question: What does toe-in mean in the wheel alignment of a vehicle?
solution:
The correct answer is __Wheels inclined inward at front.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Toe-in__ is a term used in vehicle wheel alignment.
 
• It refers to the situation where the front of the wheels are closer together than the rear of the wheels.
 
• This adjustment helps improve straight-line stability and reduce tire wear.
 
• Toe-in settings are commonly used in vehicles to optimize handling and performance.
 
• Excessive toe-in can cause increased tire wear on the outer edges of the tires.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Toe-out:**

 
 
• This is the opposite of toe-in, where the front of the wheels are farther apart than the rear.
 
• It is used in specific scenarios to improve cornering stability.
 
 
 
• **Camber Angle:**
 
 
• It refers to the tilt of the wheels inward or outward when viewed from the front of the vehicle.
 
• Positive camber means the top of the wheel is tilted outward, while negative camber means it is tilted inward.
 
 
 
• **Caster Angle:**
 
 
• The caster angle is the tilt of the steering axis when viewed from the side.
 
• It affects the vehicle's steering stability and cornering performance.
